channel.title: Mobile Dev Memo — titles & links
channel.description: Mobile Dev Memo posts by Eric Seufert — title, summary and link only. Tap through to mdm.co to read the full post (subscriber login).

item.title: GEM v2 and the financial implications of scaling laws
item.description: Meta’s GEM foundation model utilizes scaling laws to drive predictable improvements in ad ranking. By distilling complex models into efficient versions, Meta has achieved significant gains, including an 18.9% conversion uplift. Architectures like LLaTTE and Kunlun support the financial logic of continued infrastructure investment.

item.title: Podcast: Understanding Shopify’s Shop strategy (with Jess Jacobs)
item.description: Shopify leverages first-party data and unified identity to transform its Shop app from a utility tool into a merchant-centric discovery engine.

item.title: Amazon’s Everything Index
item.description: Amazon’s World Product Graph seeks to index global retail data, positioning the platform as a universal e-commerce discovery destination. By integrating external products into AI agents, Amazon challenges search rivals while controlling user data through unique identifiers, securing its role as a critical nexus for online shopping.

item.title: Conditions for agentic commerce
item.description: Third-party agentic commerce succeeds in categories defined by direct retailer fulfillment, low advertising risk, and high preference clarity.

item.title: Meta’s Europe problem (part 2)
item.description: Meta faces decelerating revenue growth in Europe due to less personalized advertising and regulatory pressures. The proposed Digital Fairness Act threatens mobile gaming monetization, potentially further reducing ad spend. These challenges, alongside AI Act compliance costs, indicate significant friction for technology firms navigating the European Union’s evolving digital landscape.

item.title: Monetizing multi-turn chatbot conversations
item.description: Chatbots leverage multi-turn interactions to refine user intent for better ad targeting. Operators must navigate an optimization dilemma: showing ads early with limited data versus waiting for more context while risking conversational termination. Success involves weighing immediate revenue against the impact on conversational hazard and future engagement value.

item.title: How big is Google’s AdMob?
item.description: Alphabet’s Network segment achieved growth in Q3 2026, ending a 17-quarter decline. This shift was fueled by AdMob, which generated an estimated $3.1 billion in quarterly revenue. Despite AdSense declines, AdMob’s 5.9% annual growth highlights its resilience within the mobile in-app advertising market, even as the broader segment remains vestigial.

item.title: Reddit Q3 2026 earnings: Reddit pulls up the logged-in drawbridge
item.description: Reddit faces declining US user growth as search referral traffic drops due to Google’s AI Overviews. The company is transitioning to a logged-in only model and shifting marketing spend toward app install campaigns. This strategy prioritizes high-value engagement and data protection over broad web reach to sustain monetization.

item.title: Apple’s identity-resolution block is not ATT for the web
item.description: Apple is blocking identity-resolution services in WebKit via dynamic rules, a move distinct from ATT as it does not favor an Apple ad network.

item.title: Meta Q3 2026 earnings: interpreting early Muse metrics
item.description: Meta’s Q3 2026 earnings reveal accelerating ad prices and the rapid adoption of Muse, which reached 10 million setups. Early metrics indicate strong commercial intent, particularly in shopping and travel. While currently subscription-based, Muse is positioned to eventually integrate into Meta’s core advertising infrastructure.

item.title: Meta’s GenRecs Tokenization and the generative retrieval opportunity
item.description: Meta is implementing GenRecs Tokenization to replace arbitrary item identifiers with Semantic IDs. This enables generative retrieval, where LLMs predict content by treating user history as a sequence of tokens. The system improves performance for new content, reduces latency, and has already delivered a 0.35% lift in conversions.
